title: Short Stuff: Dog Suicide Bridge
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Overton Bridge in Dumbarton, Scotland, nicknamed the "dog suicide bridge," where dogs have repeatedly leapt about 50 feet into a ravine. Covers the reported number of deaths, the 2010 call to animal behaviorist David Sands, his theories (scent of mink urine, an optical illusion from the bridge's design and foliage), local ghost explanations (the White Lady of Overton, a father who threw his baby off the bridge, the Celtic "thin place" idea), and the Rainbow Bridge pet myth. The hosts conclude the mystery remains unsolved.
topics: Paul Owens Baron of Rainbow Bridge

segments.title: Opening banter and Edinburgh dog story
segments.summary: Hosts open the short episode with banter, including a story about meeting a friendly dog on a walk in Edinburgh, and set up the Overton Bridge mystery.

segments.title: Overton Bridge and the dog deaths
segments.summary: Description of the stone Overton Bridge in Dumbarton, Scotland, which crosses a roughly 12-meter (about 50 ft) drop into a ravine. It was built in the mid-nineteenth century to connect Overton House to town. Locals consider it a haunted death bridge because dogs have been leaping off it since the 1950s; reported counts vary, with one website claiming about 600 and at least 50 documented, and some dogs survived and jumped again.

segments.title: Dumbarton Council calls in David Sands
segments.summary: In 2010 the Dumbarton Council asked animal behaviorist David Sands to investigate. The town's prevailing local theory was the ghost of the White Lady of Overton. Sands concluded the dogs were not jumping on purpose, and the hosts say animal suicide is considered uniquely human; they note the lemming myth has been debunked.

segments.title: Optical illusion and mink urine theories
segments.summary: Sands proposed that the bridge's tapered edges and surrounding foliage create an optical illusion making it look like a dog could run off onto level ground, when a wall actually lies below. He also suggested smells, specifically mink urine, could drive scent hounds crazy. A local hunter denied mink were present, but a Scottish official said there are mice, squirrel and mink nests nearby. Hosts note these theories don't explain why this bridge alone has the problem.

segments.title: Supernatural legends and the thin place
segments.summary: Hosts discuss supernatural explanations: a legend that a thirty-two-year-old father threw his baby off the bridge believing it was the Antichrist, with some saying the dogs jump from that spot; the Celtic concept of a 'thin place' where the spirit and human worlds overlap; and author Paul Owens's book The Baron of Rainbow Bridge, which mixes in the Rainbow Bridge pet myth.
topics: Paul Owens Baron of Rainbow Bridge

segments.title: Rainbow Bridge pet myth discussion
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Rainbow Bridge idea of pets going to an afterlife and whether dogs could intentionally end their lives. They agree the mystery remains unsolved.

segments.title: Sign-off and sponsor line
segments.summary: Hosts close the short episode, saying the mystery remains, and mention iHeartRadio.
